change: No muscle data changed. Primary (Quads all 3, glutes Maximus+Medius, Calves Lateral+Medial) and secondary (Hamstrings, abs, Triceps) confirmed correct by EMG research: quads and glutes are primary drivers with significant gastrocnemius activation; triceps hold isometric elbow extension against sled handles. Category (Free Weights), equipment (kettlebell), trackingMode (timed) all valid.

Forearms secondary changed from [Wrist Flexors, Wrist Extensors] to [Wrist Flexors] only — rope pulling is a gripping/flexion-dominant action; Wrist Extensors are not meaningfully recruited in this movement. Added Lats->Rotator Cuff as a new secondary entry: research confirms rotator cuff stabilizes the shoulder joint during rope pulls, consistent with CLAUDE.md rule for pulling exercises. All other muscles confirmed: Lats/mid back/biceps primary; Posterior Deltoid and abs secondary are correct per research.

No muscle data changed. Primary (Lats, mid back, Quads, glutes) and secondary (biceps, Hamstrings, abs, Lower Back) confirmed correct: sled drag backward engages quads and glutes as prime movers; rowing the handles drives lats, rhomboids, upper traps; biceps assist the row; hamstrings and erector spinae stabilize. Category (Free Weights) with equipment (other) is a slight mismatch per dropdown rules — other does not map to Free Weights — but no closer category exists; flagged as uncertainty.

Glutes secondary changed from [Gluteus Maximus, Gluteus Medius] to [Gluteus Maximus] only — Gluteus Medius is a hip abductor/internal rotator; in the full front split (Hanumanasana), it is not a significant active stabilizer. Gluteus Maximus actively extends the back leg hip to hold the pose. The psoas/iliopsoas (primary hip flexor stretched in the back leg) cannot be mapped to any allowed bucket+advance term and is omitted — flagged for user awareness. All other muscles confirmed: Hamstrings and Adductors primary (stretched under load); Quads->Rectus Femoris secondary (stretched on back leg, active on front for stability).

No muscle data changed. Primary (abs, Quads, glutes) and secondary (shoulders Anterior Deltoids, Triceps, Hamstrings, Calves) confirmed correct by research. Hip flexors (psoas) are also significantly engaged but cannot be mapped to an allowed bucket+advance term — omitted and flagged. Obliques provide minor anti-rotation stabilization but the bilateral symmetric jump makes them a low-priority inclusion; omission is acceptable.
